article.articleHeadline: Hanoi: Hundreds of influenza cases admitted to hospital each week.
article.articleSummary:
- Influenza activity in Hanoi, Vietnam, remains high, with Hanoi CDC reporting 200–300 influenza admissions weekly. The National Hospital for Tropical Diseases notes rising influenza admissions among both children and adults, while Hanoi’s National Children's Hospital and National Pediatric Hospital warn of serious complications. About half of pediatric inpatients in the Hanoi Children's Infectious Diseases ward have influenza; roughly 100 children daily undergo rapid testing, with 10–20% requiring hospitalization. Early symptoms include fever, cough, and runny nose; some patients, especially the elderly with comorbidities, progress to pneumonia or respiratory distress. Influenza A is emphasized as potentially severe, particularly for those with COPD, diabetes, heart disease, cancer, or rena
- Influenza A can progress to severe disease without high fever. In Hanoi, Vietnam, patients at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases and the National Children’s Hospital show that elderly individuals with hypertension or prior stroke can develop severe pneumonia and respiratory failure, with rapid tests confirming influenza A and some requiring oxygen therapy (FiO2 40-50%) or prolonged ventilation. A COPD patient with fever around 38°C deteriorated to respiratory failure needing endotracheal intubation. These cases demonstrate that fever magnitude is not a reliable severity marker; preexisting airway inflammation and comorbidities heighten risk. In September 2026, a previously healthy 4-year-old girl developed acute necrotizing encephalopathy after influenza A, despite resuscitation. 
- Ho Chi Minh City reports a sharp rise in acute respiratory infections, with 34,664 cases in week 40, up over 64% from the four-week average. Influenza is driving the surge, with 151 positive samples; influenza A/H1N1 2009 accounts for 116 cases (about 77%). The increase follows seasonal change and school return. Elderly people and those with underlying conditions are at higher risk of severe disease. National Children’s Hospital reported severe pediatric influenza A, with some deaths and a rare acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) in children aged 2–5. Adults with hypertension or COPD have developed pneumonia and require intensive care. - Severe malaria with multi-organ failure in a 46-year-old man who returned from Congo, Africa. He developed prolonged jaundice after his return. He self-medicated with traditional/herbal remedies instead of seeking hospital care. Only after developing altered mental status did he require mechanical ventilation, and he was diagnosed with severe malaria with multi-organ injury. The case underscores the danger of under-recognition of malaria in travelers from malaria-endemic regions and the need for early clinical suspicion and prompt treatment, including laboratory confirmation, to prevent organ damage and irreversible coma. Clinicians are reminded to consider malaria in febrile travelers from Africa and to avoid delays in definitive care.

article.articleHeadline: In Russia, a suspected monkeypox outbreak: five Russians were hospitalized near Moscow.

Their condition is satisfactory, and the Moscow Oblast health ministry says the situation is under control. This follows a February outbreak in the region, when an infected man was hospitalized in Domodedovo, with five contacts, and two weeks later two tourists arriving in Saint Petersburg from Thailand were diagnosed. Monkeypox spreads via close contact, including bodily fluids and contaminated objects; incubation is five to 21 days. Common symptoms include fever, swollen lymph nodes, and a painful rash.

article.articleHeadline: Understanding the Plague, an Age-Old Disease That Still Requires Vigilance.
article.articleSummary: Plague (Yersinia pestis) remains a vigilance concern. While rumors about a Russian lab incident circulated, Russia’s government attributed deaths to pneumonia with an unconfirmed cause, and Indonesian experts caution against speculative links. In Indonesia, there is no confirmed human plague outbreak; however, Y. pestis persists in wild rodents, notably rats, maintaining a potential reservoir. Plague transmission is primarily via fleas from infected rodents, direct contact with infected animal fluids, or droplets. Pneumonic plague, the most severe form, affects the lungs and can spread between animals and humans, and among people through droplets. The article emphasizes an ongoing, latent risk of plague and urges cautious interpretation of information, while noting the need for vigilance regarding any outbreaks in the region, including Indonesia. Published date: 2026-10-15.

article.articleHeadline: Avian Influenza Spreads in Sinjai, Health Office Warns of Risk of Transmission to Humans.
article.articleSummary: Avian Influenza (AI) outbreaks in Sinjai Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, have killed 5,380 poultry across eight districts and 27 villages as of October 13, 2026. Sinjai Utara accounts for the majority, with 4,624 dead birds, followed by Sinjai Timur (274), Sinjai Barat (147), Sinjai Bulupoddo (105), Tellulimpoe (104), Sinjai Borong (96), Sinjai Tengah (30), and Sinjai Selatan (6). Health authorities warn AI can transmit from poultry to humans, though not all infected birds pose a spillover risk. Human symptoms range from fever, cough, sore throat, and runny nose to shortness of breath, conjunctivitis, muscle pain, and headache; severe cases may involve pneumonia and respiratory distress. Preventive measures include avoiding contact with sick or dead poultry, using PPE when handling suspect birds, thorough handwashing, and ensuring chicken and eggs are cooked thoroughly.

article.articleHeadline: Now AI Can Predict Surges in Dengue Fever Cases.
article.articleSummary: Researchers at the Center for Tropical Medicine, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, have developed ExplainDengue, an AI-based surveillance tool that forecasts dengue fever surges. The system employs a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network to learn how dengue dynamics unfold over time and across areas. By merging dengue case data with weather and climate variables, vegetation density, and geographic features, ExplainDengue produces risk maps identifying zones most susceptible to spikes. The model captures temporal shifts and inter-regional linkages, enabling earlier warning of outbreaks and more precise targeting of public health responses. This work demonstrates the potential of integrating multi-source environmental and epidemiological data to enhance dengue surveillance in Indonesia.

article.articleHeadline: Severe air pollution from Indonesian wildfires; over 280,000 cases of respiratory tract infections in the past two months; authorities release dry ice to counter the smog (Reported by He Yongwei)

Palangka Raya city in Central Kalimantan is shrouded in orange haze, with Kalimantan's air quality triple the dangerous level. The fires, fueled by El Niño and the traditional slash-and-burn farming method, have scorched about 900,000 hectares nationwide this year. Authorities have deployed artificial rain attempts and military firefighting; on Thursday President Prabowo ordered helicopter-dropped 1.5 tons of dry ice in South Sumatra to break up smog and improve visibility, though experts say relief is local and limited. article.articleHeadline: Government's Efforts to Eradicate Snail Fever in Central Sulawesi
article.articleSummary: Schistosomiasis (snail fever) is endemic to Central Sulawesi in the Napu and Bada highlands of Poso Regency and the Lindu highlands of Sigi Regency. The government pursues eradication through mass preventive treatment in endemic villages, targeted control of the snail intermediate hosts, periodic prevalence surveys, and enhanced laboratory diagnosis using ELISA, plus a roadmap for elimination. In Poso, surveillance includes six-month stool testing in two regional laboratories and regular snail assessments at transmission sites. Community involvement includes Wuasa village (Lore Utara District) with prevention activities and school-based education that includes drug administration. At the desa level, the Gadar Basis teams (Gerakan Sadar Berantas Sistosomiasis) monitor high-risk points, promote prevention, and help maintain environmental controls. These coordinated measures aim to eliminate snail fever in Central Sulawesi.

article.articleHeadline: Impact of the 2026 Prolonged Drought: Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) Cases in Blitar Jumped 78 Percent
article.articleSummary: Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) cases in Blitar Regency, East Java, rose sharply in 2026, reaching 29,352 cases through week 40 (Sept 28–Oct 4), up 77.9% from the same period in 2025 (16,496). Health officials attribute the surge to an extended dry season, with very dry conditions worsening symptoms and reducing community immunity; air pollution from drought may also contribute. ARI is caused by viral and bacterial infections affecting parts of the respiratory tract from the nose to the lungs. The weekly peak occurred in week 38 (Sept 14–20) with 1,211 cases; week 37 in 2025 had 713. Growth began in week 31 (July 27–Aug 2) with 809 cases, rising to the week-38 peak, then easing slightly in weeks 39 (1,182) and 40 (1,134). Public health guidance includes staying hydrated, wearing masks outdoors, regular physical activity, and consuming fruits and vegetables, alongside environmental health measures.

article.articleHeadline: AI optimizes the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
article.articleSummary: On 15 October 2026, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, health workers combating Ebola Bundibugyo have digitized community health notebooks using Anthropic’s Claude model to track illness, contacts, and movements before diagnosis. The data feed, supported by CEPI, WHO Africa Regional Office, and INRB, enables one-hour situational reports instead of a full day, guiding outbreak assessment and targeted logistics such as moving medical supplies to high-risk hubs. AI aims to speed evaluation of spread and sharpen response, though experts warn about reliability, explainability, and whether clinicians truly benefit. WHO Africa's Marie Roseline Darnycka Belizaire says the faster reports are crucial. WHO Academy’s Thomas Zapata frames AI as a facilitator to reduce workload and integrate with existing systems, not a replacement for patient care. CARE’s Cecilia Mbaca stresses three questions: can AI assist medical decisions, handle repetitive tasks, and steer care more precisely? The episode underscores trust gaps in local health systems.

article.articleHeadline: How terrifying is pneumonic plague? A Russian female employee dies after suspected infection; without treatment, it could be fatal in as little as one day, and can be transmitted from person to person.
article.articleSummary: In Siberia, Russia, a 28-year-old laboratory technician at the Institute of Anti-Plague Research died after severe pneumonia on Oct 1–2. Authorities have not confirmed Yersinia pestis (plague) infection; tests found no microbe linked to her work, and the cause remains pneumonia of unknown origin. About 200 people who may have interacted with her are under medical observation; the hospital where she was treated has been quarantined, with other facilities restricting activity. WHO is monitoring and public risk is considered low. Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, can spread via respiratory droplets and progresses rapidly: untreated patients may die within about one day after severe symptoms; early antibiotics are highly effective, and close contacts usually receive seven days of preventive therapy. The disease persists in Africa, Asia, and the Americas; 2019–2025 reports show 3,847 cases and 423 deaths, dominated by the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar; the US sees sporadic cases. Sources: Bloomberg, Taiwan MOH.

article.articleHeadline: Health Priority - Ebola Outbreak in the DRC: Case Management, Contact Tracing, Research and Prevention.
article.articleSummary: Five months after the Ebola outbreak was officially declared on 15 May 2026 in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, the 17th outbreak now involves seven provinces in the northeast. The Bundibugyo strain, noted for its lethality, underpins a comprehensive response centered on case management, contact tracing, vaccination campaigns, surveillance, community sensitization, and research. Ongoing efforts include post-exposure prophylaxis trials (EBOPEP) and intensified survivor follow-up, alongside strengthened treatment centers (CTEs) and rapid laboratory confirmation. The response emphasizes early isolation, tracing of contacts, and protection against further spread, with the World Health Organization declaring the event a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The program features experts René-Hubert Mendo'o Medjo (IMT Congo), Dr Jepsy Yango (INRB) coordinating the EBOPEP prophylaxis trial, and Dr Nana Mimbu (MSF) epidemiologist in the field.

article.articleHeadline: The World Factory - With its aid to the Ebola outbreak, China extends its influence over health authorities.
article.articleSummary: Five months into the Democratic Republic of the Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak, China provides substantial aid—financial backing and medical personnel—to support outbreak response, underscoring its expanding role in African health emergencies. The article notes prior Chinese aid during a Senegal Ebola case in 2014, part of a broader soft-power strategy that increasingly positions China as a preferred partner in global health, even as it outpaces the United States in some popularity surveys. It highlights tensions from Covid-19 surrounding Wuhan, but observes improving cooperation with the World Health Organization under Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. With the U.S. departing WHO, China has become the largest public donor and seeks WHO leadership, arguing for multilateralism, while placing representatives in FAO and ICAO to offset U.S. disengagement and influence global health governance.

Since the outbreak began, Tchomia has recorded 82 confirmed cases and 36 deaths. Four patients were discharged from the Ebola Treatment Center (ETC) at Kasenyi, signaling progress but authorities urge continued vigilance. Tchomia borders Lake Albert and Uganda and is among the major hotspots alongside Rwampara, Bunia, and Mongbwalu. No new cases were notified between September 24 and October 15, 2026, following joint government and international partner efforts. Dr. Hervé Bavi, health zone medical chief, cautions against false security and urges that any symptomatic person seek care at the ETC, with free treatment. Preventive measures remain essential: regular handwashing, avoiding contact with the sick or their bodies, and immediate reporting of suspected cases to health facilities to prevent resurgence.

Participants will consider forming a multisectoral collaboration framework around the program, developing health-focused trainings tailored to Tshopo’s needs, and fostering private and community health initiatives and related actions.

article.articleHeadline: Strengthening use of Inactivated Polio Vaccines (IPVs) in Routine Immunization and Outbreak Response - GPEI
article.articleSummary: SAGE October 2026 recommendations on inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) use in routine immunization and outbreak response: countries with fewer than three IPV doses should switch promptly to a three-dose IPV-containing schedule, delivering the third dose preferably via hexavalent vaccines. If a poliovirus outbreak persists beyond six months after an initial fractional or full IPV dose, a second IPV dose in outbreak response may be considered to boost mucosal immunity, with a short-to-medium-term program evaluation. IPV remains the only vaccine protecting against all three poliovirus serotypes and type 2, which is currently most prevalent in circulation; modelling shows median type 2 immunity among under-fives at ~60% in 2025, ~70% by 2031 under the two-dose schedule, below the ~80% transmission-protection threshold. A third IPV dose could raise end-of-series immunity to ~99% with a 6-10-14 week schedule (vs ~78% with fewer doses), with largest gains in high-risk settings like Nigeria, DRC, Pakistan, and Chad. Hexavalent co-formulation is preferred for reducing visits and costs; ~40 Gavi-eligible countries are expected to switch, Mauritania and Senegal have started. Supply is projected sufficient: IPV and hexavalent capacity exceed demand; ~55 million additional doses/year across 40+ high-risk countries, timing is critical to ensure lead times and reach unvaccinated children.

article.articleSummary: Isiro, Democratic Republic of the Congo — A second training session for media professionals on Ebola communication and community engagement was held in Isiro, Haut-Uélé Province, in northeastern DRC. Organizers welcomed the journalists' ongoing daily work in raising awareness and supporting control efforts since the outbreak began, and called for regular sessions to deepen media capacity across Isiro and other Haut-Uélé territories. Thirty journalists attended this second series, underscoring the emphasis on accurate information dissemination to support the fight against Ebola.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo: Kasai - Health Professionals Launch a General Strike Amid the Spread of Monkeypox
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Kasai province faces a monkeypox surge as health professionals launch a general strike on October 15, 2026, threatening to suspend services until demands are met. The walkout occurs amid rising monkeypox cases across multiple health zones in Kasai. By the end of September, authorities reported more than 1,000 confirmed monkeypox cases and about 20 deaths in the province. Striking workers demand eight months of arrears on salaries/ordinary allowances, twelve months of unpaid supplementary allowances, and resolution of pay issues for roughly 826 Sofibanque staff, plus payroll mechanization and formal status with risk-allowance alignment for new units. They also seek better administrative and social conditions and payroll arrangements for Sofibanque employees. Reopening of services depends on full arrears payment, payroll mechanization, risk-allowance alignment, and civil-service status for new units, with ongoing concerns about outbreak response and patient care.

article.articleHeadline: ScienceNet - Research reveals the attack-and-defense mechanisms between African swine fever virus and its host.
article.articleSummary: African swine fever virus (ASFV) interaction with the host was elucidated by researchers at the Harbin Veterinary Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Heilongjiang Province, China. In vivo and in vitro experiments show endoplasmic reticulum autophagy (ER-phagy) mediated by a key receptor degrades ASFV capsid protein, inhibiting capsid assembly and exerting antiviral effects. ASFV counters this defense by molecular mimicry, hijacking the autophagy system to promote degradation of the receptor, thereby antagonizing the antiviral response. The study highlights a novel host–virus arms race mechanism and positions ER-phagy as a potential antiviral target against ASFV, informing future antiviral agent development. Published in Advanced Science (doi: 10.1002/advs.77741), with funding from the National Natural Science Foundation of China, Heilongjiang Provincial Natural Science Foundation, and the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences Youth Innovation Program.

article.articleHeadline: Can alcohol kill Norovirus? The September 2026 science field rumor list is here →
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-15, the article debunks a rumor that alcohol can kill Norovirus. It clarifies that Norovirus is highly contagious with a winter peak from October through March, causing outbreaks in schools and childcare settings. Norovirus is a non-enveloped virus; alcohol-based sanitizers and wipes have little effect, whereas handwashing with soap and running water remains essential. Transmission occurs via contaminated hands and surfaces; recommended hygiene includes washing before meals, after using the restroom, after handling food, and after contact with public objects. After infection, individuals should rest at home and isolate; they may return to school/work only after vomiting/diarrhea have resolved for 72 hours. Medical care should be sought for dehydration signs. The article also lists other rumor debunks on unrelated health topics.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue virus infection - Nature Reviews Disease Primers
article.articleSummary: High global dengue burden driven by Aedes-borne transmission across tropical and subtropical regions, with 105–390 million infections and 50–100 million symptomatic cases annually; fatality rate ~0.07% in 2024. Dengue largely affects urban centers; spread extends to continental Europe, southern USA, southern China, Argentina and Australia. Primary vector is Aedes aegypti; A. albopictus supports transmission at temperate margins. Vector-control strategies include reducing mosquito density or interfering with DENV–mosquito interactions. Wolbachia-based approaches can reduce population abundance and vector competence via male-offspring inviability, or by releasing Wolbachia-infected females so offspring are refractory; effectiveness varies by climate and environment, and costs are high. Potential paradox: reduced population immunity could raise large outbreaks; vaccination is needed for sustainable prevention. The burden includes about 5 days of work lost per case, 2.1 million DALYs per year, and US$10 billion in annual costs; Europe reports small clusters (2–200 locally transmitted cases) since 2010.

article.articleHeadline: Aminopeptidase N is a receptor for hedgehog merbecoviruses
article.articleSummary: ErinCoVs, hedgehog merbecoviruses related to MERS-CoV, use hedgehog aminopeptidase N (APN) as an entry receptor—the first demonstration that a betacoronavirus can employ APN. ErinCoVs have been detected in hedgehogs across France, the United Kingdom, China, Italy, Poland, Russia and Portugal, with hedgehog infection rates ranging from about 10% in the UK to around 60% in Germany and Italy. Using MerbecoType pseudotypes, researchers found ErinCoV spike receptor-binding domains mediate entry into cells expressing hedgehog APN; human APN or hedgehog DPP4/ACE2 do not support entry. Entry is enhanced by trypsin and validated in replication-competent Vesicular Stomatitis Virus systems with ErinCoV-12-19 spike in Vero-81 and Huh-7.5 cells expressing hedgehog APN. Co-expression of TMPRSS2 with hedgehog APN increases entry. This receptor-based finding clarifies species barriers and provides a molecular framework to assess whether ErinCoVs pose a threat to humans, informing surveillance in urban hedgehog habitats.

article.articleHeadline: Novel Cholera-Relative Strain ST2040 Emerges in Coastal China Without
article.articleSummary: Xiamen, coastal China reports a novel Vibrio cholerae non-O1/non-O139 sequence type ST2040 (HL2601), isolated from the blood of a 56-year-old man with biliary tract infection–associated bacteremia. The patient had poorly controlled diabetes, heavy alcohol use, and biliary abnormalities; no cholera-like diarrhea. NOVC strains are common in brackish waters and can cause extraintestinal illness, including bacteremia, especially in high-risk patients. China has rising NOVC bacteremia along the coast; 2005–2019 data show 82 cases with substantial mortality. HL2601’s genome is 4.3 Mbp across 50 contigs, 99.98% complete; ANI confirms V. cholerae (≈98% to N16961). It lacks major toxigenic loci (ctxAB, tcp) but carries 136 chromosomal virulence genes, including type II/VI secretion systems, RTX toxin cluster, hlyA, and iron-uptake systems. It is susceptible to imipenem, third-generation cephalosporins, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, TMP-SMX; no plasmid-borne resistance detected.

article.articleHeadline: Before COVID, an NIH lab chief proposed making a SARS-like bat virus better at infecting people
article.articleSummary: Newly released NIH records show Vincent Munster, chief of the virus ecology unit at Rocky Mountain Laboratories in Hamilton, Montana, proposed inserting a furin cleavage site into a SARS-related bat coronavirus spike to boost infectivity (email dated Oct. 6, 2019). Munster and postdoc Michael Letko had built a system to rapidly test SARS-related bat coronaviruses for human cell infection. Eleven weeks later, a coronavirus carrying a similar furin site emerged in Wuhan, China, fueling the COVID-19 pandemic. The records also show requests for unpublished bat coronavirus spike sequences—including two from the PREDICT program (Malaysia; Uganda and Rwanda)—but the sequences are too distantly related to SARS-CoV-2 to explain its origin. The work used synthetic gene fragments, not live viruses, and there is no evidence Rocky Mountain Labs possessed SARS-CoV-2 or communicated with Wuhan researchers. Letko declined comment; Munster has pleaded not guilty to mpox-related charges.

article.articleHeadline: Simple Five-Point Score Predicts 28-Day Death Risk in Children With Septic
article.articleSummary: Single-center retrospective study at Shanxi Children’s Hospital, Taiyuan, China, reviewing 123 pediatric septic shock patients admitted to PICU from 2020–2024, with 28‑day mortality of 83/123 (67.5%). Researchers developed the Septic Shock Clinical Score System (SCSS) to predict 28‑day death within 24 hours of PICU admission. Four predictors retained by LASSO: mechanical ventilation, use of ≥2 vasoactive agents, troponin T >40 ng/L, and prothrombin time >18 seconds; each dichotomized and combined into a 0–5 point score. The SCSS achieved strong discrimination (AUC 0.902, 95% CI 0.839–0.965) and favorable calibration on bootstrap validation. When stratified, mortality was 23.8% for low-risk, 90.0% for intermediate-risk, and 90.9% for high-risk groups. The approach emphasizes bedside applicability without complex equations, potentially guiding early risk stratification for pediatric septic shock in similar settings.

article.articleHeadline: DNA Test Outperforms Standard Assays in Head-to-Head HIV Diagnosis Trial
article.articleSummary: In a Beijing head-to-head HIV diagnostic study, 215 adults seeking their first test (June 2024–May 2025) were evaluated on four platforms: ELISA for antibody/P24, Abbott RealTime HIV-1 RNA quantification, a qualitative multiplex RNA assay, and a quantitative proviral DNA assay on lymphocyte-enriched cells (copies per million nucleated cells). Using a composite gold standard, 102 were HIV-positive and 113 negative. Proviral DNA achieved 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (AUC 1.000). RNA quantification: 99.02% sensitivity, 100% specificity (AUC 0.995). ELISA: 99.02% sensitivity, 2 false positives (specificity 98.23%, AUC ~0.923). Qualitative RNA: 28 false positives (specificity 75.22%). One RNA false negative occurred with recent ART suppression; proviral DNA remained positive. Pre-analytical RNA stability issues and a Hook effect likely contributed to ELISA misclassification. Globally, UNAIDS 2024 reports 40.8 million people living with HIV; China has 1.35 million with ~100,000 new cases in 2024, underscoring the push to move nucleic-acid testing to the center of diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Teachers, Not Students, May Be the Overlooked Face of School Tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Pulmonary tuberculosis in Chengdu, southwestern China, shows divergent trends between students and teachers from 2010–2024. General population TB fell from 61.78 to 35.63 per 100,000 (−42.3%). Teachers showed a flat trend with zero joinpoints; annual percent change −2.19% (95% CI −5.04 to 0.75; P=0.130), effectively no significant decline. Students had two joinpoints (2017, 2021) with: 2010–2017 −7.11%/yr; 2017–2021 −1.41%/yr; 2021–2024 −17.32%/yr. By 2024, teacher rate 16.00/100k vs student rate 5.78/100k, a 2.77-fold difference. The parallel trends null was rejected (P=0.005), indicating distinct trajectories. Sensitivity analysis excluding 2020–2022 (COVID years) yielded −3.53%/yr for teachers and −7.22%/yr for students, with no significant parallelism (P=0.206). Conclusion: focusing school TB screening on students may overlook teachers, suggesting need to rebalance screening resources and management in schools.

article.articleHeadline: Avian influenza in Autumn 2026: What is known about the risk to humans and what to do if you find a dead bird.
article.articleSummary: As of 15 October 2026, autumn migration raises avian influenza risk to poultry and people. WHO/ECDC assess population risk as low; no sustained human-to-human transmission. Globally, 15 human cases have been reported this year: 1 H5N1 in Bangladesh and 1 in Cambodia; 13 H9N2 in China. In Europe, 110 avian infections (June–August 2026) were detected: 103 in wild birds, 7 in domestic poultry. For the general public, EU risk remains low; for poultry workers and hunters, risk ranges from low to moderate. A notable imported case occurred in spring 2026 in Italy (H9N2) from Senegal; no secondary cases. WHO notes properly cooked poultry and eggs are safe. Guidance: house poultry in enclosed quarters, segregate species, avoid contact with wild waterfowl, disinfect facilities, buy birds from vetted sources, report dead wild birds to veterinary services, and wash hands after contact. Seek medical care for fever, respiratory symptoms, or conjunctivitis after exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Targeted Sequencing Outperforms Smears in Spotting Hidden Lung Infection
article.articleSummary: In a real-world China study from Chifeng Municipal Hospital (Inner Mongolia), 941 patients with suspected lower respiratory tract infections underwent bronchoscopy with BALF and were split into metagenomic NGS (mNGS, DNA-only) in 479 and targeted NGS (tNGS, DNA+RNA) in 462. Against a multidisciplinary final diagnosis, mNGS sensitivity 90.6%, specificity 21.4%, PPV 97.4%; tNGS sensitivity 73.4%, specificity 14.3%, PPV 96.5%. tNGS uncovered pathogens missed by conventional tests, including 54 Mycobacterium tuberculosis cases (smear/NAATs missed 42; smear false negatives 77.8%), and Pneumocystis jirovecii (silver staining falsely negative in 80%). Polymicrobial infections were common in tNGS positives (93.5% multiple pathogens; cross-kingdom co-infections 32.6%; Streptococcus pneumoniae with HHV-7 in 30 cases; Klebsiella pneumoniae with S. pneumoniae in 25). Treatment changes followed results: mNGS positives led to escalation in 39.9% (184/461); tNGS positives in 22.6% (77/341).

article.articleHeadline: Machine Learning Model Predicts Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis Risk in
article.articleSummary: IPA risk in non-neutropenic ICU patients in China: 837 adults with pulmonary infections across three tertiary hospitals (Dec 2020–Dec 2025). A Random Forest model with external AUC 0.865 identified six dominant predictors by SHAP: isolation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, PaO2/FiO2 <200 mmHg, diabetes mellitus, SOFA >5, lymphopenia (<0.8×10^9/L), and ICU admission; corticosteroid exposure did not rank in the top six. Stratified by bacterial context, corticosteroids showed an OR of 0.52 (95% CI 0.214–1.283) in P. aeruginosa infections and 2.17 (95% CI 0.722–6.535) in other Gram-negative infections (P for interaction 0.131). A six-variable bedside score (Pseudomonas isolation 3; PaO2/FiO2<200 2; diabetes 1; SOFA>5 1; lymphopenia 1; ICU admission 1) yields 0–9 points; ≥4 high risk. Training/internal/external AUCs: 0.869/0.774/0.719. Survival analysis: non-pseudomonal Gram-negative infections had higher mortality, showing context-dependent risk.

article.articleSummary: RSV rising among young children in Bac Ninh, Vietnam. RSV typically starts with cough, runny nose, and mild fever but can progress to bronchiolitis, pneumonia, or respiratory failure in infants, premature infants, and children with underlying conditions. Parents should monitor breathing rate, feeding, and overall alertness; seek urgent care if rapid breathing, chest indrawing, cyanosis, poor feeding, or lethargy occur. Preventive measures include frequent handwashing with soap, cleaning toys and surfaces, avoiding close contact with people with respiratory symptoms, maintaining well-ventilated living spaces, and avoiding cigarette smoke. There is no routinely used specific antiviral; treatment is supportive and guided by clinical assessment and risk factors.

article.articleHeadline: Measles is making a comeback. Will we end it for good?
article.articleSummary: Measles is resurging in the Western Pacific, threatening elimination by 2030. The region, home to 2.2 billion people, once saw measles nearly eliminated due to decades of political commitment and routine immunization, but the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccine misinformation have widened immunity gaps. Since 1974, global vaccination saved around 154 million lives; measles vaccination accounts for about 94 million, including 12 million in the Western Pacific. Nine countries—Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Mongolia, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, and Viet Nam—still aim to eliminate by 2030; WHO-certified measles and rubella elimination in all 21 Pacific island countries and areas occurred in 2025. In 2025, more than 1.6 million Western Pacific children were zero-dose. Achieving elimination requires strong routine immunization, robust surveillance, rapid outbreak response, and sustained political and financial commitment, with vaccines delivering up to $54 in social returns per dollar.

article.articleHeadline: Fungal Genomes Reveal Why a Maize Pathogen Dominates Ear Rot and Poisons
article.articleSummary: Maize ear rot in Karnataka, southern India, is dominated by Fusarium verticillioides, comprising 43 of 54 isolates (79.63%) from diseased ears across six Fusarium species. Pathogenicity tests showed high virulence (disease severity >75%); F. verticillioides reduced seed germination to 65% and F. graminearum to 62%, with notable stalk/ear rot symptoms. Toxin-genome linkage revealed universal fumonisin potential in F. verticillioides, with FUM1 present in all 43 isolates; LC-MS confirmed high fumonisin accumulation in kernels. F. graminearum carried trichothecene genes (TRI7/TRI13), indicating NIV-type chemotypes. Whole-genome sequencing of PMER18 produced a ~40 Mb genome with 98.0% BUSCO completeness, shedding light on the molecular basis of dominance. The integrated approach (morphology, multilocus phylogenetics, toxin-gene screening, LC-MS, genomics) links ecological prevalence to toxin potential, underscoring fumonisin-related food-safety risks in Karnataka maize.

article.articleHeadline: Central team reviews LSD control measures in J&K livestock
article.articleSummary: On 15 October 2026, a central expert team led by Dr Sudam Bagh visited Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD)–affected areas in Jammu and Kashmir, including Samba, Kathua and Jammu districts, to review control measures. The team distributed mineral mixtures, wound-dressing materials and disinfectants and held awareness programmes for farmers on biosecurity, hygiene and livestock management. Samples from LSD-affected cattle in Samba, Kathua and Jammu were collected to support laboratory investigations. LSD is a contagious viral infection of cattle and water buffalo caused by Capripoxvirus; it does not affect humans. Transmission occurs mainly through blood-feeding insects and movement of infected animals, with symptoms such as high fever (>41°C), firm skin nodules (2–5 cm), swollen lymph nodes, leg edema, reduced milk yield, weight loss and possible infertility. Control relies on live-attenuated vaccines, vector control, quarantine and movement restrictions, with strengthened Centre–State coordination.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue threat in Delhi; safety precautions to take when using mosquito repellents.
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports a dengue surge with 98 new cases in the week ending Oct 3 and 104 more by Oct 10, totaling 799 cases as of Oct 13. Aedes aegypti mosquitoes are active in daytime amid intermittent rains and humidity. Use EPA-approved repellents: DEET 10–30%, picaridin, IR3535, or lemon eucalyptus oil. Do not use lemon eucalyptus or para-menthane-diol on children under 3; pregnant individuals may use DEET, picaridin, or IR3535. Children over two months may use up to 30% DEET. Apply repellent to exposed skin after sunscreen; avoid rubbing into makeup; avoid combination sunscreen-repellent products. Expected protection: DEET/IR3535 6–8 hours; picaridin/lemon eucalyptus 4–6 hours; reapply after sweating or rain. Monsoon precautions in Delhi: wear long sleeves, track pants, socks; use a fan; keep windows screened and sleep under nets; permethrin-treated clothing/gear (not skin); empty water from containers every two days. Seek care for high fever, severe headache, vomiting, bleeding; prefer paracetamol over ibuprofen/aspirin.

article.articleHeadline: Viruses From Sewage Turn Bone Cement Into a Weapon Against MRSA Implant
article.articleSummary: Six bacteriophages (φRAGS1, φRAGS8, φRAGS15, φRAGS21, φRAGS37, φRAGS47) showed broad lytic activity against MRSA clinical isolates, with φRAGS15 lysing all 17 strains. Phages were isolated from hospital sewage and environmental water around Varanasi (Ganga/Yamuna/Sangam region). They were combined with carbonate-intercalated Mg2+/Al3+ layered double hydroxide nanoparticles at 1% by weight in poly(methyl methacrylate) bone cement (nanoLDH-PMMA). In a rabbit prosthetic‑joint infection model, 24 female rabbits received distal femoral implants; MRSA (5×10^6 CFU) was injected on day 6. Phage therapy (10^12 PFU/mL, 15 μL/kg) was given subcutaneously on days 12, 15, 18 around the implant. Untreated and conventional cement groups showed progressive cortical erosion; the nanoLDH cement group exhibited osteolysis, reactive sclerosis and sequestrum formation, signaling a gradient toward chronic infection. The study supports phage‑augmented, biocompatible implants for MRSA prosthetic infections.

article.articleHeadline: UP Finds 57 Microbiologically Unsafe Packaged Water Samples In Statewide Drive
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-15, Uttar Pradesh's FSDA tested 242 packaged drinking water samples in a week-long drive, finding 57 microbiologically unsafe and 146 substandard. Unsafe samples contained E. coli, coliforms, yeast and mould, signaling possible biological contamination; substandard samples failed one or more prescribed quality requirements. Unsafe results appeared in 39 districts, with Ghaziabad and Hapur recording four unsafe samples each; Gautam Buddha Nagar and Ayodhya three each; Lucknow one. Substandard failures were more widespread, led by Chandauli with 12, then Ayodhya, Barabanki, Ghaziabad and Jaunpur with eight; Kanpur Nagar seven; Agra and Bareilly six; Prayagraj and Varanasi five. FSDA ordered licence suspensions and production halts for units with unsafe water; five batches of 1,000 bottles each must pass before production resumes. Substandard units have one week to rectify and must pass three batches; possible action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Commissioner Roshan Jacob directed verification and enforcement.

article.articleHeadline: Absconding rape suspect bites cop during chase, turns out HIV+

The arrest followed a tip that placed the man in the area in connection with another case. SP Rajat Saklecha confirmed the HIV result. The suspect was later taken to hospital for further assessment and treatment, while authorities monitor for potential exposure to the constable. No death toll is reported; the incident raises concerns about exposure risk in law enforcement encounters.

article.articleHeadline: Takeda Joins Hands With Karnataka Leaders to Call for Year-Round Dengue Preparedness as Climate Change and Urbanization Reshape Dengue Risk
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Karnataka, India is framed as a year-round public health threat as climate change and rapid urbanization reshape transmission. Bengaluru hosted the multi-stakeholder dialogue 'From Awareness to Action: Advancing Dengue Prevention in Karnataka,' which endorsed a 4-Point Call-to-Action to shift from seasonal outbreak responses to continuous year-round preparedness. Participants included Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India, Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader Fareed, School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa, Dr. Rajani M. (Director, Health & Family Welfare SIHFW), Dr. Mahender Nayak (Takeda), and other state representatives. Karnataka has recently seen a decline in dengue cases, but experts warn ongoing drivers—environmental conditions, rising temperatures, and urban expansion—pose future outbreak risks. The strategy emphasizes a Whole-of-Society approach (Janabhāgitva), tying surveillance, diagnostics, vector monitoring, vaccination, and community-based prevention together, with Takeda supporting science-informed, year-round dengue management and immunization options where safe and beneficial.

article.articleHeadline: PMC conducts night blood survey for filariasis
article.articleSummary: Two-month night blood survey for lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) underway in Pune, India. Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) launched the drive targeting construction sites and migrant laborers, with blood samples collected between 9 pm and midnight. The campaign involves 12 teams (six from PMC, six from state health department); each health inspector will deploy five ward-staff to collect samples. Pune reports only seven old cases and is not endemic, but officials worry migrant workers from higher-prevalence states could introduce transmission. The survey seeks early detection and timely treatment to prevent local spread. Lymphatic filariasis is transmitted by female Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes; infection can be silent for years. When mature (5-18 months), adult female worms can live 10-15 years, causing elephantiasis, genital complications, disability, stigma, and economic burden.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria cases spiral, become more severe; docs advise early treatment
article.articleSummary: Mumbai reports a surge in malaria this year, with cases more severe and daily ICU admissions in both public and private hospitals. Doctors note falciparum and vivax infections causing organ involvement, including kidneys and liver, and at least two malaria deaths in Mumbai plus the nursing student death at JJ Hospital on Oct 4. Official monsoon totals show 7,422 cases June–August, a 44% rise from 5,144 last year, though practitioners warn the true burden is higher due to under-reporting by private clinics. In Dharavi, several GPs see about seven malaria patients each, and delays in diagnosis coupled with self-medication fueled by AI-based online information are concerns. Possible drivers include construction work. Treatment emphasis is on completing the full anti-malarial course and managing comorbidities; adherence to state protocols and BMC surveillance is urged.

article.articleHeadline: Anthrax infection kills female elephant in Coimbatore forest; carcass burnt

Carcass burnt on October 15, without opening, per standard protocol, with handlers wearing personal protective equipment. Forest and Animal Husbandry Departments have stepped up vigilance against the disease following confirmation. No details on infection source or additional cases are provided. The incident highlights ongoing wildlife health surveillance in Coimbatore forest areas.

article.articleHeadline: Depts told to coordinate to curb monkey fever in Narasimharajapura
article.articleSummary: Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD), or monkey fever, is a concern in Narasimharajapuram taluk, Chikkamagaluru district, Malnad region, with 54 cases last year. An inter-departmental meeting led to a coordinated plan across health, forest, animal husbandry, panchayat, and education departments as monsoon wanes and summer begins. Transmission occurs via infected ticks; monkey deaths are a precursor. Human-to-human spread is not reported. The health department will conduct fever surveys, collect blood samples for lab testing; ticks from forests have been sent for analysis. A One Health community surveillance system is established to monitor cases. Government provides free treatment upon confirmation. Precautions include avoiding areas with dead monkeys, applying tick-prevention measures, washing exposed skin after forest visits, and seeking immediate care for fever, headache, body pain, red eyes, or vomiting.

article.articleHeadline: In Kerala, IAV's novel system to predict the spread of dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Kerala's dengue early warning system, developed by the Institute of Advanced Virology (IAV) in Thiruvananthapuram, uses machine learning to predict district-level dengue transmission. Led by Dr. Abhinand C.S. from the Virus Genomics, Bioinformatics and Statistics division, the system fuses rainfall, temperature, ambient humidity, and reported dengue cases to generate weekly district alerts, identifying risk as low, moderate, high, or very high. Trained on six years of daily data (Mar 2020–Feb 2026) from state health surveillance and the Central Meteorological Department, it also accounts for Aedes mosquito biology and climate variability. Preliminary evaluation using health data from March–July 2026 shows predicted trends closely match reported cases. Authorities caution that ongoing testing is needed across districts and climate scenarios. The tool is designed to augment, not replace, existing surveillance, guiding vector-control intensification, public awareness, and prioritized resource allocation where risk is highest.

Breeding sources are dominated by water containers (buckets, jars, pots); routine inspections and water removal reduce Aedes density.

article.articleHeadline: Stop Rabies expands to Siargao, strengthening community partnerships for rabies prevention
article.articleSummary: Stop Rabies expands to Siargao in October 2026 to strengthen rabies prevention through education, vaccination, mass dog and cat vaccination, spay/neuter activities, and responsible pet ownership. The Philippine rollout is a Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health initiative with the GARC Rabies Alliance, in partnership with local governments, schools, veterinarians, and community groups. Since launching in the Philippines, Stop Rabies has operated in Luzon and the Visayas, including Puerto Galera, Marinduque, Laguna, and Negros Occidental. Education efforts reach thousands of students—over 2,300 in Puerto Galera and more than 8,000 in Los Baños (11 schools)—plus rabies awareness activities in Bacolod City and Victorias City. Rabies remains fatal but preventable, with about 300–400 deaths annually and roughly four million animal bites nationwide. The program supports vaccination campaigns and prompt post-exposure action, aiming to eliminate human deaths from dog-mediated rabies by 2030, in line with World Rabies Day.

article.articleHeadline: Months of Hallucinations Led Doctors to Tapeworm Cysts in a Woman's Brain, and Pork Wasn't How She Got Them
article.articleSummary: Neurocysticercosis from pork tapeworm eggs infected a 52-year-old woman in the Philippines, presenting four months of headaches and visual hallucinations, then speech and naming difficulties. Brain MRI/CT showed cysts in multiple lobes and the cerebellum, each with a bright dot—the scolex—producing the pathognomonic dot-in-hole sign. EEG revealed epileptiform discharges on the left posterior cortex, linking hallucinations to seizures. Infection arises from swallowing tapeworm eggs shed in human feces, not from eating pork; eggs hatch and form brain cysts, with symptoms often appearing months to years later as cysts die. She was treated with praziquantel and albendazole, glucocorticoids, and levetiracetam; steroids curb inflammation from dying cysts. After one month, symptoms resolved and cysts shrank with dots disappearing. Neurocysticercosis is common where pigs roam and sanitation is poor (Latin America, Asia, Africa) and is a leading cause of adult-onset epilepsy globally. CDC emphasizes handwashing, safe food/water, and travel history in diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Enterovirus-related medical visits dip below 10,000, but risk remains! This year, a total of 7 severe cases; Taiwan CDC urges vigilance for warning signs | LIFE Lifestyle Network
article.articleSummary: Taiwan’s week 40 enterovirus activity totaled 9,001 outpatient/ER visits (Oct 4–10), down 12.8% from 10,332, but still above baseline and below the epidemic threshold of 12,000 visits/week. The Taiwan CDC notes ongoing transmission risk; this year there have been 7 severe enterovirus infections, including 1 death. Laboratory typing shows EV-D68 predominates in recent severe cases (5), with one each of Coxsackie A4 and A16. Internationally, Vietnam reports rising enterovirus activity with 10 deaths; China shows a recent weekly uptick after earlier declines; Thailand remains variable. With World Handwashing Day on Oct 15, authorities urge rigorous hygiene in schools, daycare centers, and indoor play areas; families should practice the 5-step handwashing and regularly disinfect children's toys. Most severe risk is in children under 5; seek prompt medical care for warning signs such as lethargy, seizures, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing, or altered consciousness.

article.articleHeadline: RSV pneumonia can affect people of all ages; older adults aged 50+ with comorbidities are at risk of severe pneumonia and heart disease.
article.articleSummary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pneumonia affects all ages but poses the greatest risk to older adults, especially those 50+ with comorbidities such as heart and lung disease, kidney disease, or diabetes. RSV can cause severe pneumonia and may trigger heart failure or arrhythmias, sometimes requiring hospitalization or ICU care and oxygen or ventilation; long recovery can lead to permanent functional decline. In Thailand, RSV circulates year-round, with higher activity in the rainy and cool seasons; transmission occurs via coughing, sneezing, and close contact, including from school-age children. Elderly patients 75+ or 50+ with chronic diseases have markedly higher mortality risk than young children—up to about 10-fold. Vaccination is available for older adults, protecting both RSV A and B; recommended for those 75+ or 50+ with comorbidities, regardless of season. Preventive measures include hand hygiene, masking, distancing, vaccination planning, and consulting clinicians.

article.articleHeadline: Egg prices back in the 7,000-won range... Will price volatility rise as avian influenza spreads in winter? - Maeil Ilbo
article.articleSummary: South Korea faces potential winter spread of high-pathogenic avian influenza (AI) threatening egg supply. As of Oct 14, farm prices for 30-large eggs were 5,690 won and wholesale 5,963 won, down ~6–7% since Oct 1, while consumer prices rose to 7,045 won (+2.4%). Long-term prices have eased since July, though Oct is 3.2% higher YoY. Production is improving: laying-hen stock over six months old at 59.02 million, daily output about 50.31 million eggs, up ~0.6–0.7%. On-farm stockpiles rose to 26.9% with two-day supply. Last winter AI culled 11.34 million laying hens (13.7% of stock); recovery is projected at 6–9 months. Wild birds at Han River estuary, Siwha Lake and Sapgyo Lake surged; 31 of 62 AI outbreaks occurred on laying farms. Government enforces a four-stage biosecurity regime Oct–Feb and diversifies imports from Thailand, Brazil, and Denmark after US disruptions (Brazil: ~1.12 million eggs; 30-egg unit 43,923 won).

article.articleHeadline: Heat 5°C above average increases hospitalizations of children due to infection by 22% | Portal Band
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-15, Brazil-wide study across 1,814 municipalities (over 78% of the population) finds that every 5°C rise in daily mean temperature increases by 22% the risk of hospitalizing children for gastrointestinal infections in the following nine days. The new dossier 'El Niño: impact of climate change on adult and child health' was presented to physicians at the Brazilian Pediatric Congress and sponsored by Opella. Infants under 1 year bear the highest risk, with water- and foodborne infections showing the strongest association with higher temperatures. Climate extremes contribute via drought-related water scarcity and flood-related contamination of water supplies and foods, as well as shifts in the gut microbiota. Regional variation: the North and Northeast are more affected by drought and heat, while the South faces floods that disrupt potable water. Preventive guidance emphasizes hydration, hygiene, and seeking care for dehydration.

article.articleHeadline: PAHO classifies the risk of measles transmission in South America as 'very high' after a surge in cases in 2026.
article.articleSummary: PAHO/OPAS classifies the risk of measles transmission in South America as very high amid a 2026 surge. From January 4 to October 3, 2026, 55,792 measles cases and 77 deaths were reported in 17 countries/territories, about 4.8 times higher than the same period in 2025. The outbreak reflects vaccination gaps and potential amplification during large religious gatherings in Argentina, Peru, and Uruguay; Brazil reports at least 39 cases. Guatemala leads infections, followed by Mexico, the United States, Peru, and Canada; these five nations account for 99.5% of cases (≈55,500). Only about 25% of 43 reporting countries met vaccination targets; 2025 first-dose coverage was 88% and second-dose 85%. Roughly 1.6 million children in the Americas did not receive any measles vaccine in 2025. PAHO urges vaccination before travel and rapid case detection; two-dose coverage remains essential, especially for travelers.

article.articleHeadline: Porto Alegre Expands Tuberculosis Prevention for People Living with HIV.
article.articleSummary: Porto Alegre expands tuberculosis prevention for people living with HIV via the Ministry of Health's Universal TPT project. The Regional Center for Integrated Care and Prevention of STIs, HIV/AIDS and Coinfections (Craip) now performs portable chest radiographs, with artificial intelligence support to triage images and identify potential pulmonary changes, expediting the ruling-out of active TB before starting preventive therapy. On-site imaging speeds assessment and integrates with ongoing health follow-up. The city health secretary aims to consolidate the care flow and extend the strategy to other network services, including Primary Health Care, increasing access to prevention and clarifying individuals indicated for preventive therapy. The initiative targets the elevated TB risk among people living with HIV.

article.articleHeadline: Hidden Parasites Surface in Brazilian Zoo Animals in Landmark Survey
article.articleSummary: Getúlio Vargas Zoobotanical Park, Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, was the site of a parasite survey across 75 species and 409 animals. Analyzed 144 fecal samples collected from enclosure floors during December 2021, employing four coproparasitarogical methods (direct, spontaneous sedimentation, Willis flotation, Mini-FLOTAC) with two evaluators; samples preserved in 5% formalin and sent to UFERSA for analysis. Endoparasites were detected in 52.8% of samples. Among positives, nematodes dominated (80.3%), protozoa (23.7%), cestodes (13.2%), trematodes (10.5%); 26.3% showed mixed infections. Positivity by host group: reptiles 66.7%, birds 60%, mammals 47.8%. Within mammals, primates carried coccidia, Strongyloides, Bertiella, Platynosomum; carnivores had Strongyloides and Oxyuridae; even-toed ungulates with Balantioides plus whipworms and Strongyloides; odd-toed ungulates with strongyles and Balantioides; opossums hosted Eimeria, Cruzia, Aspidodera. Birds and reptiles contributed distinct entries; the work highlights hidden parasite diversity with implications for welfare, conservation, and zoo worker health. Published in Frontiers in Parasitology.

article.articleHeadline: Rise in viral infection cases worries residents of an inland city in Acre.
article.articleSummary: On 15 October 2026, Sena Madureira, an inland city in Acre, Brazil, reports a rise in people seeking care for viral infection symptoms. Viroses are viral infections that can affect different parts of the body. Symptoms commonly include fever, headache, muscle pains, fatigue, runny nose, cough, sore throat, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Transmission occurs via direct contact with infected people, respiratory droplets, contaminated surfaces, and sometimes contaminated water or food. Preventive measures include regular handwashing with soap and water, avoiding touching the face, ventilated spaces, drinking safe water, and proper food hygiene. Do not share personal items or have close contact when symptomatic. Hydration is important; avoid self-medicating with antibiotics. Those with persistent symptoms, children, the elderly, and chronically ill require heightened vigilance. Confirmation of an outbreak and specific viruses awaits official health data; seek care for severe symptoms such as shortness of breath, dehydration, confusion, or worsening condition.

article.articleSummary: Dengue prevention training for Brazil’s Unified Health System (SUS) agents delivered via a WhatsApp chatbot, launched by Takeda. The national program targets community health agents (ACS) and endemias agents (ACE) with 2,000 licenses. Mobile-based learning fits fieldwork, reducing barriers of traditional e-learning. Modules cover four axes: safe information, community-based prevention, family support, and countering misinformation, with emphasis on Aedes aegypti as dengue’s vector and reference to the Ministry of Health’s 2024 Dengue and Arboviruses Action Plan. Participation requires signing up through the Conheça a Dengue portal and providing the CNS number; completion yields a certificate for continuing education hours. Takeda will monitor usage metrics (enrollments, module progression, completion rate). The program aims to empower frontline workers who reach about 500 people each, potentially informing up to roughly one million residents nationwide.

article.articleHeadline: Dead rat inside a cake: Understand the health risks after contact with a rodent in food | abc+
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis risk after contact with a rodent in food in Porto Alegre, Brazil, linked to a dead rat found in an iFood-ordered cake from Casa de Bolos, Cavalhada unit, on Oct 14. Two customers, a 31-year-old man and a 26-year-old woman, reportedly may have ingested part of the animal; fur was found on other pieces. They required medication and were tested for leptospirosis; they will be monitored for 30 days due to the bacterium’s incubation. The bakery was closed and the owner, a 41-year-old woman, was arrested. Leptospirosis is caused by Leptospira, transmitted via urine of infected animals, especially rats; incubation 1–30 days. Symptoms range from fever and myalgias to Weil’s syndrome (jaundice, renal failure, hemorrhages). Diagnosis uses blood tests at Lacens; treatment should start on suspicion, with doxycycline or amoxicillin early, and penicillin or ceftriaxone in severe cases. Floods and poor sanitation increase risk.

Key symptoms include fever and rashes on hands, feet, and buttocks, and mouth ulcers; mouth sores can cause pain, leading to swallowing difficulties and reduced fluid intake.

article.articleHeadline: GHS begins Yellow Fever vaccination campaign in three Upper West districts

article.articleHeadline: Onion Extract Boosts Standard Therapy Against Latent Tuberculosis in Rabbit
article.articleSummary: Latent-like pulmonary infection by Mycobacterium aurum in New Zealand White rabbits was used to test Allium cepa (onion) extract as an adjunct to standard TB preventive therapy. In Kumasi, Ghana, researchers induced latency, validated by stabilized lung CFU, chest radiographs without active disease, and adaptive immune changes. During four weeks of treatment, rabbits received isoniazid plus rifapentine, onion extract (250/500/1000 mg/kg), or both. All onion-containing regimens reduced pulmonary bacterial burden vs untreated controls (P<0.0001). The combination with the highest onion dose yielded the greatest reduction: 480 CFU vs 495 CFU for uninfected controls, suggesting near-complete clearance. The study supports plant-derived compounds as adjuncts to latent TB therapy, potentially via improved drug uptake, efflux-pump inhibition, or complementary metabolic targeting; prior in vitro work showed anti-efflux and antibiofilm effects of Allium cepa extracts.

article.articleHeadline: Falling platelets track malaria parasite burden in Ghana, but only up to a
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Ghana’s Agogo cohort: platelet counts decline with age, complicating thrombocytopenia interpretation and allowing no clear sex difference, suggesting age-aware rather than sex-based thresholds. A plateau in platelet depletion emerges at high parasite densities, with Spearman r = −0.34, indicating only modest tracking of parasite burden by platelets and no further drop in severe parasitemia. Platelet metrics alone cannot diagnose malaria; a logistic model (AUC 0.771; sensitivity 63.6%; specificity 79.9% at Youden’s threshold) on a population with 10.6% positivity shows moderate discrimination and underscores use with fever history, travel/exposure, and clinical signs for triage toward microscopy. Seasonal positivity peaks in May–June during Ghana’s rainy season in forest–savanna transition zones, in a high-transmission setting (inoculation rate 40–158 bites/person/year).
